info.name: Rasayel REST API
info.description:
Welcome to the Rasayel API Documentation!

Empowering sales teams to excel in the digital age, Rasayel offers a comprehensive suite of tools tailored to enhance communication and streamline operations over WhatsApp. Our API serves as the gateway to unlocking the full potential of Rasayel's platform, enabling seamless integration with your existing systems and empowering developers to craft innovative solutions tailored to your business needs.

Getting Started

First thing you need to do before using our REST APIs is to create a new API key on Rasayel, to do this, you can head over to the API management page to create a new API key or use an existing one.

Creating a New API Key

Click on "Created your first key", which will prompt you to give your API key a name and select the authorization scope you'd like to give to the API key holder

Authorization scopes

  • Read: will only be able to do read operations through the API (fetching a template, fetching a conversation, etc)
  • Read/Write: will be able to do any operation, either a read or a write (sending a message, fetching a template, etc)

After creating the key, you will be given the API info, copy the "Basic Auth Value" which is shown in the below image, this value will be needed to be sent in the Authorization header with the requests for authentication.

Use an Existing API Key

If you want to use an existing API key instead of creating a new one, you can follow the same instructions as the above by

  • Heading to the settings
  • Navigate to the API management page
  • You'll find the created API keys listed there
  • Click on the "Reveal token" to get the API info show up, then copy the "Basic Auth Value", similar to what we did above

Authentication

To authenticate your API requests, you'll need to provide the "Basic Auth Value" that we extracted above of the API key you want to use in the `Authorization` header when sending any request.

curl --location 'http://api.rasayel.io/v1/templates?page=1&per_page=20' \
--header 'Authorization: Basic {{your_token}}'

Identifying Yourself

To specify a user to be taking actions on his behalf using the API, you can specify the ID of the user in the X_On_Behalf_Of header along with the request

curl --location 'http://api.rasayel.io/v1/templates?page=1&per_page=20' \
--header 'X_On_Behalf_Of: {{user_id}}' \
--header 'Authorization: Basic {{your_token}}'

Finding Your ID

You can find your ID by navigating to the settings followed by navigating to the profile page which you'll find your user ID in similar to the image shown below

Pagination

Query Parameters

Any Index request in our API is paginated, you can control the pagination using the following query parameters

  • page: specifies the page you want to fetch.

  • per_page: specifies the amount of records returned in a single page.

Pagination Object

Every paginated request will include a pagination object under the key pagination , you'll find an example below of the pagination object returned along with comments to specify what each field exactly indicate.

"pagination": {
    "total_count": 1337, # The total count of the records
    "total_pages": 45, # Total pages
    "current_page": 1, # The current fetched page
    "next_page": 2, # The index of the next page
    "previous_page": null, # The index of the previous page
    "first_page": true, # A boolean to specify whether this is the first page or not
    "last_page": false # A boolean to specify whether this is the last page or not
}

Rate Limit

We use rate limiting to ensure fair experience for all users of our API.

It prevents any user from overloading the system with too many requests in a short time.

How Rate Limiting Works at Rasayel

We use a method called the Leaky Bucket approach. Imagine you're filling a bucket with water. If you add water too fast, it will overflow. But if you add water at a steady pace, it won't. The same principle applies to sending requests to our API.

The leaky bucket system rewards users who send requests at a steady rate. If you send too many requests too quickly, your "bucket" overflows, and you'll be temporarily blocked from sending more requests.

Limits

Our API implements rate limits using a leaky bucket algorithm as mentioned above, each client is allocated a bucket with a maximum capacity of 100 tokens. Tokens are replenished at a fixed rate of 20 requests per minute. When a client makes a request, tokens are consumed from the bucket, and if the bucket is empty, further requests will be delayed until more tokens are available.

Tracking Your Usage

To help you monitor your API usage, each response includes a header labeled X_Rasayel_Api_Call_Capacity, indicating the number of tokens consumed out of the maximum limit. This header is presented in the format {{ tokens_used }}/{{ max_tokens_limit }}. By parsing this header, you can easily track the consumption of tokens against your allotted capacity, allowing for efficient management of your API requests and ensuring compliance with the rate limits imposed by the system.

Reaching The Limits

In the event that you encounter rate limiting, the API will include a Retry-After header in the response. This header indicates the duration, in seconds, that you should wait before attempting further requests to successfully access the API. By referencing the value provided in the Retry-After header, you can implement appropriate backoff strategies within your application, ensuring that subsequent requests are made within the allowed timeframe and minimizing disruptions to your service.

request.description:
Updates a Contact using the ID.

Response Model: Contact

Parameters

Key Type Required Description
name string false updated name of the contact
phone string false updated phone of the contact
email string false updated email of the contact
tag_ids array[integer] false updated tags of the contact
properties array[Property] false updated properties to be attached to contact

  • if tag_ids is provided, it will remove the old contact tags and apply the new specified tags, passing an empty array [] will clear out the contact tags, don't pass this parameter if you don't want the contact tags to be updated.

  • if properties is provided, it will remove the old contact properties and apply the new specified properties, passing an empty array [] will clear out the contact properties, don't pass this parameter if you don't want the contact properties to be updated.

item.name: Messages

request.description:
Sends a message to a Conversation or a Contact

Response Model: Message

Sending Options

You can send messages through our APIs using two different methods, each method differs in the parameters being passed to the request.

Below, you will find the two methods listed along with the parameters needed for each.

Using Phone Number

  • Contact's Phone Number: The phone number of the contact you're trying to reach out to.

  • Sending Channel ID: The Channel ID you want to send the message with.

Using Conversation ID

  • Conversation ID: The ID of the conversation on Rasayel you want to send the message to

Message Types

You can send various types of messages using this API, below is the list of messages you can send through this endpoint.

  • Text Message

  • Media Message

  • Note Message

  • Template Message

You'll find an example attached with the request body and the responses for each message type.

Parameters

Key Type Required Description
conversation_id integer true (if phone and channel_id aren't provided) conversation id in Rasayel to send the message in
phone string true (if conversation_id isn't provided) phone of the receiver of the message
channel_id integer true (if conversation_id isn't provided) id of the channel to send the message with
type string enum true type of the sent message
text object (text message) true (if message type is TEXT) text message object
note object (note message) true (if message type is NOTE) type of the sent message
template object (template message) true (if message type is TEMPLATE) type of the sent message
media object (media message) true (if message type is MEDIA) type of the sent message

Text Message Object

Key Type Required Description
body string true body of the text message

Note Message Object

Key Type Required Description
body string true body of the note message

Media Message Object

Key Type Required Description
caption string false caption sent with the media
url string true public url of the media to be sent
filename string true filename of the media to be stored on our servers with
  • filename: need to specify the extension of the file with the file name, eg. photo.jpg

Template Message Object

Key Type Required Description
message_template_id integer true id of the template to be used in the message
components array[component parameters] true (if the template has variables) array listing each component's parameter if the template has parameters

Component Parameter Object

Key Type Required Description
type string enum true component type, see valid component type values here
subtype string enum true (only for button component parameter object) type of the button, see valid button types enum here
button_index integer true (only for button component parameter object) index of the button the parameter is being passed to (0 indexed)
parameters array[parameter object] true array of parameters for this component (parameter object is passed for each variable in the component)
Media Parameter Object
Key Type Required Description
type string enum true media type to be sent, based on the header media format
url string true public url of the media to be sent
filename string true filename of the media to be stored on our servers with
  • Media parameters are only used for templates with MEDIA headers
Text Parameter Object
Key Type Required Description
type string enum true type of the parameter
text string true text to replace the variable
  • Type of the parameter in the Text parameter object should be passed as TEXT

first_inbound_message_at datetime datetime of first inbound message in the conversation false

last_outbound_message_at datetime datetime of last outbound message in the conversation false
last_opened_at datetime datetime that the conversation was last opened at false
last_closed_at datetime datetime that the conversation was last closed at false
assignee_id integer id of the assigned user false
assigned_team_id integer id of the assigned team false
snoozed_until datetime datetime that the conversation will be unsnoozed at if it is snoozed false
created_at datetime conversation creation datetime false
updated_at datetime conversation last update datetime false

Conversation State Enum Values

Value Description
unanswered Unanswered conversation
opened Opened conversation
closed Closed/Solved conversation
snoozed Snoozed conversation
campaign_initiated Conversation created by an initiated campaign
campaign_workflow_bot_controlled Conversation controlled by a campaign bot
proactive_workflow_bot_controlled Conversation controlled by a proactive bot

id integer id of the property true
name string name of the property true
type string enum type of the property true
description string description of the property false
editable boolean is property editable false
identifier string unique identifier of the property false
standard boolean is property one of the standerd properties false
channel_specific boolean is property a channel specific false
archived boolean is property archived false
created_at datetime contact creation time false
updated_at datetime time that the contact was last updated at false

Type

NUMBER
